description: Hi! I'm putting together a team to build the ultimate Mars Survival Guide, an interactive platform/app designed to help future Martian pioneers navigate environmental hazards, resource management (oxygen, water, radiation), and emergency protocols on the Red Planet
summary:
Maze ("Mars + Waze") is a navigation prototype by Team Orden 66 for the challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map". It answers a critical question for future crewed missions: how does an astronaut walk safely on Mars?

We built a route planner that layers NASA terrain, soil, radiation and temperature data into a single interactive map of Gale Crater. The user picks a science target near Curiosity's landing site and Maze automatically calculates the safest walking path, avoiding steep slopes, dunes and extra radiation dose, and shows why that route was chosen.

This addresses the challenge by turning separate mission datasets into one integrated, decision-ready view of a Marswalk. It matters because on Mars every step costs time, energy, oxygen and radiation exposure, and there is no GPS or internet to help. Maze works offline and helps astronauts and mission planners spend less risk and more time doing science, so every first step on another world is a safe one.
details:
Maze ("Mars + Waze") plans the safest walking route for astronauts on Mars. In our Gale Crater prototype, the user picks a science target near Curiosity's landing site and Maze computes the best path, explaining which slopes, dunes and exposure it avoids.

How it works: we combine NASA data into one cost map: HiRISE/CTX elevation models (slope), TES/THEMIS thermal inertia (loose sand vs. firm rock), Curiosity RAD (radiation) and REMS (temperature). A least-cost routing engine finds the optimal path.

Benefits: time, energy, oxygen and radiation are limited on Mars. Maze turns scattered mission data into one clear decision, reducing risk and leaving more time for science. It can support mission planning, training and education.

Creativity: we reimagined a familiar car navigation app for another planet, routing around dunes, cliffs, cold and radiation instead of traffic.

Factors considered: astronaut safety, offline-first design (no internet on Mars), traceable public NASA data, and a modular design so new regions can be added.

Tools: Python, FastAPI microservices, Rasterio, GDAL, SQLite, GeoTIFF/GeoPackage, Docker Compose, GitHub. AI assistants (Claude) helped with code, docs and the demo; Google Gemini generated the music.
